---
title: "Distance Calculation"
subtitle: Distance calculation to the nearest coastline from core locations
---

As the initial data analysis will be performed on the MUDAB sites located within European coastlines, the distances to the nearest coastline were calculated.

The distance data is available in the `dist_to_coast` column of the [survey](db-schema.qmd#survey) table.

## Methods

The distance is computed by [seastamp](https://github.com/AIQC-Hub/seastamp), the command line tool that annotates locations for every stage of the pipeline. Using one tool throughout means the pilot values agree with the ones the later generations carry, rather than differing in detail.

* **Shoreline data:** the **Global Self-consistent, Hierarchical, High-resolution Geography** ([GSHHG](https://www.soest.hawaii.edu/pwessel/gshhg/)) database at full resolution, the most detailed of its five levels.
* **Projection:** a **Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area** projection centred on the data. seastamp derives the extent from the sampling points themselves rather than applying a fixed global projection.
* **De-duplication:** coordinates are rounded to three decimal places before lookup, so surveys repeated at one position are computed once.
* **Result:** the shortest distance from the survey position to the nearest shoreline polygon, in kilometres.

::: {.callout-note}
### Recalculated at v0.1.12
These values were previously calculated in R with the [sf](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sf/index.html) library, against a GSHHG extract cropped to Europe and projected to EPSG:3035. Both approaches use GSHHG, so the distances moved only slightly: across the 2,045 distinct survey positions the median change is 0.05 km (0.2%) and the largest is 62.4 km.
:::

## Sediment Site Locations with Distances to Coast

{{< include _db-setup.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| output: false

// --- Query site locations ---
df_loc = db.query(`
  SELECT DISTINCT
     s3.survey_id,
     s3.station_latitude AS latitude,
     s3.station_longitude AS longitude,
     CASE
       WHEN s3.dist_to_coast <= 10  THEN '0 to 10km'
       WHEN s3.dist_to_coast <= 30  THEN '10 to 30km'
       WHEN s3.dist_to_coast <= 100 THEN '30 to 100km'
       ELSE '≥100km'
     END AS distance
  FROM sediment s1
  JOIN station s2 ON s2.station_no = s1.station_no
  JOIN survey s3 ON s3.survey_id = s1.survey_id
`)

// --- World boundaries (Natural Earth via CDN) ---
world_topo = fetch("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2/countries-50m.json")
  .then(r => r.json())

world_geojson = topojson.feature(world_topo, world_topo.objects.countries)

dist_counts = db.query(`
  SELECT distance AS Distance,
         COUNT(*) AS '# Sampling Sites'
  FROM (
      SELECT DISTINCT
         s3.survey_id,
         s3.station_latitude AS latitude,
         s3.station_longitude AS longitude,
         CASE
           WHEN s3.dist_to_coast <= 10  THEN '0 to 10km'
           WHEN s3.dist_to_coast <= 30  THEN '10 to 30km'
           WHEN s3.dist_to_coast <= 100 THEN '30 to 100km'
           ELSE '≥100km'
         END AS distance
      FROM sediment s1
      JOIN station s2 ON s2.station_no = s1.station_no
      JOIN survey s3 ON s3.survey_id = s1.survey_id
  ) t
  GROUP BY distance
`)

```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 620,
  height: 540,
  marginRight: 120,
  caption: "Sediment Cores — LAEA Europe Projection",
  // Pan-European + Svalbard bounding box: 25°W–35°E, 33°N–82°N
  projection: ({width, height}) => {
    const lonMin = -21, lonMax = 41
    const latMin =  45, latMax = 78
    const mercY     = lat => Math.log(Math.tan(Math.PI / 4 + lat * Math.PI / 360))
    const yTop      = mercY(latMax), yBot = mercY(latMin)
    const yRange    = yTop - yBot
    const xRange    = lonMax - lonMin   // degrees
    // Fit the tighter of width/height to avoid overflow
    const scaleH    = (height - 20) / yRange
    const scaleW    = (width  - 20) / (xRange * Math.PI / 180)
    const scale     = Math.min(scaleH, scaleW)
    const yMid      = (yTop + yBot) / 2
    const latCenter = (Math.atan(Math.exp(yMid)) - Math.PI / 4) * 360 / Math.PI
    return d3.geoMercator()
      .center([(lonMin + lonMax) / 2, latCenter])
      .scale(scale)
      .translate([width / 2, height / 2])
  },
  color: {
    domain: ["0 to 10km", "10 to 30km", "30 to 100km", "≥100km"],
    range:  ["#30123b",   "#28bbec",    "#a2fc3c",    "#fb8022"],
    legend: true,
    label:  "Distance to Coastline"
  },
  marks: [
    // Ocean background clipped to the domain frame
    Plot.frame({ fill: "#d0e8f5" }),
    // Country polygons — clip: "frame" trims anything outside the domain bbox
    Plot.geo(world_geojson, { fill: "#d4d4d4", stroke: "#888", strokeWidth: 0.4, clip: "frame" }),
    // Graticule grid lines clipped to frame
    Plot.graticule({ stroke: "gray", strokeWidth: 0.4, strokeDasharray: "3,3", clip: "frame" }),
    // Frame border drawn on top
    Plot.frame({ stroke: "#555", strokeWidth: 0.8 }),
    // Site locations coloured by distance category
    Plot.dot(df_loc, {
      x: "longitude",
      y: "latitude",
      fill: "distance",
      r: 3.5,
      fillOpacity: 0.85,
      stroke: "#222",
      strokeWidth: 0.3,
      clip: "frame"
    })
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(dist_counts, {
  columns: ["Distance", "# Sampling Sites"],
  layout: "fixed",
  width: { "Distance": "50%", "# Sampling Sites": "50%" }
})
```
